work_units.responsibility: Specify the smallest production-safe Redis visibility-timeout patch across LX-Annotate plus LuxNix

findings.claim: gc-05 used Kombu's 3600-second Redis visibility default while late-ack tasks and the configured FFmpeg interval can run for 86400 seconds.
findings.source: gc-05 deployed Celery/Kombu runtime probe; lx_annotate/settings/settings_base.py; endoreg_db/tasks.py

findings.claim: The production-safe value is 90000 seconds, exported identically as CELERY_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT, broker transport visibility_timeout, and result transport visibility_timeout, with a one-hour margin over every configured late-ack task.
findings.source: Celery Redis transport contract and gc-05 task/runtime timeout inventory

findings.claim: The missing implicit route for endoreg_db.tasks.video_hls_materialization must target ffmpeg_media.
All workers consuming Redis DB 1 must restart together after deployment because the shortest visibility timeout used by a shared broker wins.
findings.source: Celery Redis documentation and gc-05 worker topology

gaps: A 25-hour behavioral redelivery test is not practical before today's user session; effective live Kombu channel and worker configuration must be inspected immediately after deployment.
The separate explicit HLS task hard limit remains shorter than the host's maximum FFmpeg interval.

work_units.responsibility: Design an idempotent recovery procedure for gc-05 video 4 from the current fenced retry loop

findings.claim: Video 4 finalization first failed because an orphaned processed-HLS QUEUED reservation caused already_materializing while the import was still active.
findings.source: gc-05 lx-annotate journal from 2026-09-03 19:20 through 2026-09-04 09:58 CEST

findings.claim: The active upload task e1424deb38764981a5e29719b7dcd661 was a Redis-redelivered task, and obsolete processed-HLS deliveries were independently queued.
findings.source: gc-05 Celery inspection and Redis DB 1 delivery metadata

findings.claim: Non-terminating task revocation plus compare-and-set dispatch failure of the exact orphaned HLS reservations preserves the active import and deletes no media.
findings.source: endoreg_db/services/hls_media.py mark_hls_materialization_dispatch_failed and gc-05 live verification

findings.claim: The current task must remain uninterrupted and the worker must not restart until the import is terminal because revoke state is memory-only.
findings.source: gc-05 ffmpeg worker ExecStart and Celery revoked registry

gaps: The import was still processing when this work unit completed; terminal video, HLS, media, and queue acceptance gates remain orchestrator work.
Authenticated playback and annotation save/reload require a separate acceptance probe.

work_units.responsibility: Resolve the gc-05 external archive device identity plus recommend the least-risk recovery procedure

findings.claim: The archive mount is stale on absent device 8:3 while the same Seagate disk reappeared as /dev/sdb3, device 8:19.
findings.source: gc-05 findmnt, mountinfo, lsblk, udevadm, blkid, and sysfs inspection

findings.claim: The persistent archive identity is usb-Seagate_Expansion_HDD_00000000NT197WLC-0:0-part3 with ext4 UUID 96c09eae-57cb-4e5c-95e1-9050a32abcc4.
Immediate read-write remount is unsafe because the filesystem reports needs_recovery and orphan_present; stale namespaces must first be cleared and an offline read-only e2fsck performed.
findings.source: gc-05 tune2fs, findmnt, namespace, and process-reference inspection

findings.claim: One controlled video 4 recovery likely fits local NVMe capacity, but no concurrent import or reconciliation is safe until verified obsolete temporary data is cleaned.
findings.source: gc-05 df, btrfs usage, du, and active FFmpeg observations

gaps: Full physical-disk SMART telemetry is unavailable through the USB bridge.
Filesystem repair and persistent mount configuration remain separate post-import operational work.

work_units.responsibility: Audit test coverage needed to prove slow FFmpeg tasks avoid redelivery under the deployed runtime

findings.claim: The prior Endoreg visibility test was a false positive for gc-05 because LX-Annotate production settings omitted the timeout settings.

Application tests must exercise a non-default 93600-second sentinel through production settings and the real lx_annotate Celery app, verify integer equality across all three settings, reject malformed values, and compare against registered late-ack task limits.
LuxNix must type and propagate visibilityTimeoutSeconds into every application and worker environment and fail evaluation below the FFmpeg-plus-margin threshold.
findings.source: LuxNix lx-annotate role, service options, environment script, and Nix evaluation contract

findings.claim: Post-deployment app, Kombu connection/channel, and live worker-conf inspection can prove the effective threshold immediately without waiting 25 hours.

gaps: Immediate configuration inspection is not a black-box 25-hour redelivery test.
A disposable NixOS worker-loss and Redis-interruption convergence test remains future readiness work.
